```json
{"rows": [
{"n": 1, "label": "requested", "why": "\"`PUT /tickets/:id/assignee` with a JSON body `{\"assignee\": \"<agent>\"}`... an agent is a non-empty name of at most 64 characters\" and \"`GET /tickets` gains an `assignee` filter\"."},
{"n": 2, "label": "requested", "why": "\"The agent a ticket is assigned to is notified that it was assigned to them\"; using the outbox and a template only decides how that notification is delivered."},
{"n": 3, "label": "requested", "why": "\"Every ticket shows its `assignee` (null when unassigned)\" and \"Everything the service already does keeps working\" cover persisting the field and preserving the existing audit."},
{"n": 4, "label": "implied", "why": "Existing stored tickets have no assignee field, so \"Every ticket shows its `assignee` (null when unassigned)\" and existing behaviour would break unless old records read as null."},
{"n": 5, "label": "implied", "why": "Assign, unassign and the no-op on the same agent must not race or produce duplicate notifications, and keeping the existing synchronous store ordering ensures that without adding anything new."},
{"n": 6, "label": "requested", "why": "\"an agent is a non-empty name of at most 64 characters\"; the rest relies on existing HTTP boundaries and adds no new access control."},
{"n": 7, "label": "implied", "why": "A failed assignment notification must be visible to whoever acts on it, and reusing the existing audit and outbox reports does this without a new channel."}
]}
```
